waterQuality.title: Water Quality

waterQuality.phDesc: Measures water acidity or alkalinity on a scale of 0 to 14. Normal drinking water is between 6.5 and 8.5.
waterQuality.turbidityDesc: Measures cloudiness caused by suspended particles. Values above 5 NTU indicate potential sediment or microbial contamination.
waterQuality.tdsDesc: Total Dissolved Solids measures inorganic salts and organic matter. Desirable limit is under 500 ppm.
waterQuality.temperatureDesc: Water temperature affects chlorine efficacy and bacterial growth.

steps.step1Content: This dashboard displays your village’s current health-risk information and water safety surveillance status. The circular gauge highlights your community’s overall risk score and whether estimated conditions are Low, Medium, High, or Critical. (Note: These are automated surveillance risk estimates to aid early warning, not confirmed medical diagnoses).
steps.step1Tip: Check this risk score regularly. If it transitions to High or Critical, check active alerts for immediate household precautions.
steps.step2Content: Here you can quickly report water or symptom issues in your village, view nearby village risk levels on the map, review active alerts, or check water quality observations with a single tap.
steps.step2Tip: Reporting suspected symptoms like diarrhea, fever, or vomiting quickly helps community health workers investigate potential contamination before it spreads.
steps.step3Content: Learn how to read available water-quality readings for your village. We monitor pH (acidity level), Turbidity (water clarity), TDS (dissolved minerals & salts), and Temperature. Clear status badges indicate whether each reading is Normal, Moderate, or Needs Attention.
steps.step3Tip: Elevated turbidity or TDS often indicates runoff, silt, or pipe contamination. Scroll down this page to view 7-day, 30-day, and 3-month water trends.
steps.step4Content: View AI-generated risk predictions and understand the displayed risk level. AquaShield combines water test parameters, symptom reports, and seasonal data to predict potential water-borne disease threats (such as Diarrhea, Typhoid, or Cholera) and display protective drinking-water advisories.
steps.step4Tip: These predictions are proactive warning estimates to help you take timely action—such as boiling drinking water or reporting unusual symptoms—before an outbreak occurs.
steps.step5Content: Ask questions anytime about water safety, purification methods, boil-water advice, or water-borne disease symptoms. Your AI Health Assistant provides safe, plain-language guidance 24 hours a day.
steps.step5Tip: Try asking: “How should I treat well water?” or “What should I do if a family member has diarrhea?”
steps.step6Content: Whenever an official boil-water advisory, contamination warning, or disease alert is issued for your area, a red badge will light up here. Click the bell to view instant summaries or open the Alerts tab for full guidance.
steps.step6Tip: Active critical alerts will also appear prominently in red or amber banners across your home dashboard.
steps.step7Content: You have completed the tour orientation! Access all sections of the application from the sidebar navigation. If you ever need a refresher or want to explore these steps again, click this Tour Guide button anytime.
steps.step7Tip: You can also check your registered village, update your profile, or adjust notification preferences in the My Profile tab.
